snapshot.stmt: For every \(P\in\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon}\), consistency, conditional exchangeability, and fixed overlap identify \(V^\star(P)=\sum_{x=1}^dp_x\max\{\mu_{0x},\mu_{1x}\}\). defs.def:global-extension: For \(u\in\mathbb R_+^4\) with \(s(u)>0\), define \(g_{a,\epsilon}(u):=s(u)u_{a1}/\max\{s_a(u),\epsilon s(u)\}\) and \(\bar f_\epsilon(u):=\max_{a\in\{0,1\}}g_{a,\epsilon}(u)\); set \(g_{a,\epsilon}(0)=\bar f_\epsilon(0)=0\).

snapshot.stmt: For every fixed \(0<\epsilon<1/2\), there is \(C_\epsilon<\infty\) such that the explicit all-data estimator \(\widehat V_{n,d}^{\mathrm{JF}}\) satisfies \(\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon}}E_P[(\widehat V_{n,d}^{\mathrm{JF}}-V^\star(P))^2]\leq C_\epsilon\min\{1,d/[n\log(ed)]\}\) for every \(n\geq1\) and \(d\geq2\). defs.def:jackson-factorial-estimator: Put \(L_d=\log(ed)\), \(m=n/8\), and \(K_d=\max\{2,\lfloor\kappa L_d\rfloor\}\). Otherwise draw \(M\sim\operatorname{Pois}(n/4)\), and on \(M\leq n\) mark the first \(M\) observations independently by \(B_i\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(1/2)\), producing independent pilot and evaluation counts \(N'_{\jmath,x}\) and \(N_{\jmath,x}\); on \(M>n\), set the randomized output to zero. For \(M\leq n\), let \(c_{\jmath,x}=N'_{\jmath,x}/m\), \(h_{\jmath,x}=H_0\{\sqrt{c_{\jmath,x}L_d/m}+L_d/m\}\), \(\ell_{\jmath,x}=\max\{0,c_{\jmath,x}-h_{\jmath,x}\}\), \(u_{\jmath,x}=c_{\jmath,x}+h_{\jmath,x}\), and \(Q_x=\prod_{\jmath\in\mathcal J}[\ell_{\jmath,x},u_{\jmath,x}]\), with center \(b_x\) and coordinate radii \(r_x\). Expand \(P_{x,K_d}(v)-\bar f_\epsilon(b_x)=\sum_\alpha b_{x,\alpha}((v-b_x)/r_x)^\alpha\). In the Jackson branch define the all-data estimator \(\widehat V_{n,d}^{\mathrm{JF}}:=E[\widetilde V\mid O_1,\ldots,O_n]\), where the conditional expectation integrates only the displayed auxiliary Poisson count and marks.

defs.def:empirical-ratio-estimator: Let \(\overline N_x=\sum_{i=1}^n\mathbf 1\{X_i=x\}\), \(\overline N_{ax}=\sum_{i=1}^n\mathbf 1\{X_i=x,A_i=a\}\), and \(\overline S_{ax}=\sum_{i=1}^n\mathbf 1\{X_i=x,A_i=a,Y_i=1\}\). defs.def:jackson-kernel: For integer \(K_d\geq2\), let \(J_{K_d}(t)=c_{K_d}[\sin(K_dt/2)/\sin(t/2)]^4\) on \([-\pi,\pi]\), with removable values filled continuously and \(c_{K_d}\) chosen so that \(\int_{-\pi}^{\pi}J_{K_d}(t)\,dt=1\). snapshot.stmt: Every \((\mathbf P,\mathbf Q)\in\Delta_d^2\) mapped by \(\mathrm{def:l1-embedding}\) yields a law in \(\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon}\) with \(p_x=(P_x+Q_x)/2\), \(\pi_x=1/2\), and \(V^\star(P)=1/2+\lVert\mathbf P-\mathbf Q\rVert_1/4\). defs.def:observed-model-class:
\(\mathcal D_{d,\epsilon}^{\mathrm{obs}}\) is the set of all laws \(\mathbb P\) on \([d]\times\{0,1\}^2\) for which there are \(p=(p_1,\ldots,p_d)\in\Delta_d\), \(\pi_x\in[\epsilon,1-\epsilon]\), and \(\mu_{ax}\in[0,1]\) satisfying, for every \(x\in[d]\) and \(a\in\{0,1\}\),
\[
 q_{a1,x}=p_x\pi_x^a(1-\pi_x)^{1-a}\mu_{ax},\qquad
 q_{a0,x}=p_x\pi_x^a(1-\pi_x)^{1-a}(1-\mu_{ax}),
\]
where \(q_{ay,x}=\mathbb P(X=x,A=a,Y=y)\).  Thus the support contains at most \(d\) covariate cells; the parameters on a null cell may be chosen arbitrarily within their displayed ranges.
defs.def:observed-optimal-value: For \(\mathbb P\in\mathcal D_{d,\epsilon}^{\mathrm{obs}}\) with table \(\mathbf q=(q_x)_{x=1}^d\), define the observed-law optimal-regression functional by \(\Psi(\mathbb P)=\Psi(\mathbf q):=\sum_{x=1}^d p_x\max_{a\in\{0,1\}}\mu_{ax}\).  This value is independent of the permitted choice of \(\mu_{ax}\) on cells with \(p_x=0\).

assumptions.ass:iid-sampling: For each \(\mathbb P\in\mathcal D_{d,\epsilon}^{\mathrm{obs}}\), \(O_1,\ldots,O_n\) are independent and have common law \(\mathbb P\).
assumptions.ass:fixed-overlap: For every \(\mathbb P\) under consideration and every \(x\in[d]\) with \(p_x=\mathbb P(X=x)>0\), the conditional probability \(\pi_x=\mathbb P(A=1\mid X=x)\) satisfies \(\epsilon\leq\pi_x\leq1-\epsilon\).

snapshot.stmt:
For every fixed \(0<\epsilon<1/2\), there are constants \(0<c_\epsilon\leq C_\epsilon<\infty\) such that, for every \(n\geq1\) and \(d\geq2\),
\[
c_\epsilon\min\{1,d/[n\log(ed)]\}\leq\mathfrak R_{n,d,\epsilon}
\leq\sup_{\mathbb P\in\mathcal D_{d,\epsilon}^{\mathrm{obs}}}E_{\mathbb P}[(\widehat V_{n,d}^{\mathrm{JF}}-\Psi(\mathbb P))^2]
\leq C_\epsilon\min\{1,d/[n\log(ed)]\}.
\]
Through \(\mathrm{prop:causal-optimal-value-corollary}\), the same risk frontier applies to the causal optimal-treatment value over all causal completions whose observed margins range over \(\mathcal D_{d,\epsilon}^{\mathrm{obs}}\).

snapshot.stmt: Along arbitrary sequences \(n\to\infty\) with \(d=d_n\geq2\), uniform consistency for estimating \(\Psi(\mathbb P)\) over \(\mathcal D_{d,epsilon}^{\mathrm{obs}}\) is possible if and only if \(d=o(n\log(en))\). defs.def:global-extension: For \(u\in\mathbb R_+^4\) with \(s(u)>0\), define \(g_{a,\epsilon}(u):=s(u)u_{a1}/\max\{s_a(u),\epsilon s(u)\}\) and \(\bar f_\epsilon(u):=\max_{a\in\{0,1\}}g_{a,\epsilon}(u)\); set \(g_{a,\epsilon}(0)=\bar f_\epsilon(0)=0\).
defs.def:empirical-ratio-estimator: Let \(\overline N_x=\sum_{i=1}^n\mathbf 1\{X_i=x\}\), \(\overline N_{ax}=\sum_{i=1}^n\mathbf 1\{X_i=x,A_i=a\}\), and \(\overline S_{ax}=\sum_{i=1}^n\mathbf 1\{X_i=x,A_i=a,Y_i=1\}\). Put \(\widehat p_x=\overline N_x/n\), \(\widehat\mu_{ax}=\overline S_{ax}/\overline N_{ax}\) with \(0/0=0\), and \(\widehat V_{n,d}^{\mathrm{ER}}=\sum_{x=1}^d\widehat p_x\max_a\widehat\mu_{ax}\).
defs.def:jackson-kernel: For integer \(K_d\geq2\), let \(J_{K_d}(t)=c_{K_d}[\sin(K_dt/2)/\sin(t/2)]^4\) on \([-\pi,\pi]\), with removable values filled continuously and \(c_{K_d}\) chosen so that \(\int_{-\pi}^{\pi}J_{K_d}(t)\,dt=1\). For a rectangle \(Q_x=\prod_{\jmath\in\mathcal J}[\ell_{\jmath,x},u_{\jmath,x}]\) with center \(b_{\jmath,x}=(\ell_{\jmath,x}+u_{\jmath,x})/2\) and radius \(r_{\jmath,x}=(u_{\jmath,x}-\ell_{\jmath,x})/2\), define \(P_{x,K_d}\) by the even product convolution \(P_{x,K_d}(b_x+r_x\odot\cos\theta)=\int_{[-\pi,\pi]^4}\bar f_\epsilon(b_x+r_x\odot\cos(\theta+t))\prod_{\jmath\in\mathcal J}J_{K_d}(t_{\jmath})\,dt\).

assumptions.ass:iid-sampling: For each \(\mathbb P\in\mathcal D_{d,\epsilon}^{\mathrm{obs}}\), \(O_1,\ldots,O_n\) are independent and have common law \(\mathbb P\).

snapshot.stmt:
For every fixed \(0<\epsilon<1/2\), there are constants \(0<c_\epsilon\leq C_\epsilon<\infty\) such that, for every \(n\geq1\) and \(d\geq2\),
\[
c_\epsilon\min\{1,d/[n\log(ed)]\}\leq\mathfrak R_{n,d,\epsilon}
\leq\sup_{\mathbb P\in\mathcal D_{d,\epsilon}^{\mathrm{obs}}}E_{\mathbb P}[(\widehat V_{n,d}^{\mathrm{JF}}-\Psi(\mathbb P))^2]
\leq C_\epsilon\min\{1,d/[n\log(ed)]\}.
\]
Through \(\mathrm{prop:causal-optimal-value-corollary}\), the same risk frontier applies to the causal optimal-treatment value over all causal completions whose observed margins range over \(\mathcal D_{d,\epsilon}^{\mathrm{obs}}\).

defs.def:minimax-risk: \(\mathfrak R_{n,d,\epsilon}:=\inf_{\widehat V}\sup_{\mathbb P\in\mathcal D_{d,\epsilon}^{\mathrm{obs}}}E_{\mathbb P}[(\widehat V(O_1,\ldots,O_n)-\Psi(\mathbb P))^2]\), where the infimum is over all measurable maps from \(([d]\times\{0,1\}^2)^n\) to \(\mathbb R\).
defs.def:observed-model-class:
\(\mathcal D_{d,\epsilon}^{\mathrm{obs}}\) is the set of all laws \(\mathbb P\) on \([d]\times\{0,1\}^2\) for which there are \(p=(p_1,\ldots,p_d)\in\Delta_d\), \(\pi_x\in[\epsilon,1-\epsilon]\), and \(\mu_{ax}\in[0,1]\) satisfying, for every \(x\in[d]\) and \(a\in\{0,1\}\),
\[
 q_{a1,x}=p_x\pi_x^a(1-\pi_x)^{1-a}\mu_{ax},\qquad
 q_{a0,x}=p_x\pi_x^a(1-\pi_x)^{1-a}(1-\mu_{ax}),
\]
where \(q_{ay,x}=\mathbb P(X=x,A=a,Y=y)\).  Thus the support contains at most \(d\) covariate cells; the parameters on a null cell may be chosen arbitrarily within their displayed ranges.
defs.def:observed-optimal-value: For \(\mathbb P\in\mathcal D_{d,\epsilon}^{\mathrm{obs}}\) with table \(\mathbf q=(q_x)_{x=1}^d\), define the observed-law optimal-regression functional by \(\Psi(\mathbb P)=\Psi(\mathbf q):=\sum_{x=1}^d p_x\max_{a\in\{0,1\}}\mu_{ax}\).  This value is independent of the permitted choice of \(\mu_{ax}\) on cells with \(p_x=0\).

assumptions.ass:fixed-overlap: For every \(\mathbb P\) under consideration and every \(x\in[d]\) with \(p_x=\mathbb P(X=x)>0\), the conditional probability \(\pi_x=\mathbb P(A=1\mid X=x)\) satisfies \(\epsilon\leq\pi_x\leq1-\epsilon\).
